assets.sourceBrief: Potted plants and armchair seating arranged beside floor-to-ceiling windows in a reception lobby.

assets.transcriptText: (A) Curtains are being drawn across the lobby windows. (B) Receptionists are checking guests in at the front desk. (C) Armchairs are positioned near large windows in a waiting area. (D) A carpet is being rolled out along the hallway.
When will the revised budget spreadsheet be ready for review? (A) By three o’clock this afternoon. (B) In the third-floor conference room. (C) Yes, the accounting team approved it.
Where should I leave the signed supplier contracts? (A) Before next Tuesday’s deadline. (B) On Ms. Pham’s desk in the legal office. (C) They were signed by the regional director.
Who is leading the onboarding session for the new interns tomorrow? (A) Mr. Hoang from Human Resources. (B) At nine-thirty in the morning. (C) Yes, all six interns attended.
Why was the client presentation postponed until Friday? (A) For about forty-five minutes. (B) Because the lead consultant is traveling today. (C) The slide deck has sixteen pages.
How did you resolve the issue with the inventory software? (A) I installed the latest patch from the support portal. (B) Every Monday morning at eight o’clock. (C) About two hundred units in stock.
Which catering package did the event committee select? (A) The vegetarian buffet with seasonal fruit. (B) At the riverside convention center. (C) Around eighty guests have confirmed.
Have the replacement printer cartridges arrived yet? (A) The reception desk just signed for the parcel. (B) Please print double-sided copies. (C) To the stationery supplier in District Three.
Could you proofread the press release before I send it to the media list? (A) Sure, share the document link with me. (B) The press conference was well attended. (C) No, it was published last month.

Would you prefer to take the morning train or fly out on Wednesday evening? (A) The morning train gives us more time to prepare. (B) Platform four at the central station. (C) Yes, my flight was on time.

The safety inspection for the laboratory is scheduled for Thursday, isn’t it? (A) Actually, it was moved to next Monday. (B) Remember to wear safety goggles. (C) Dr. Nguyen works in the research wing.
Didn’t you receive the updated seating chart for the seminar? (A) No, let me check my spam folder. (B) The chairs are very comfortable. (C) About fifty participants per session.

The air-conditioning in the west wing feels unusually warm this afternoon. (A) Building maintenance is already checking the thermostat. (B) Yes, the weather forecast predicts rain. (C) About twenty degrees Celsius last winter.

Would you like me to help you set up the audio equipment for the webinar? (A) Thanks, I still need to test the wireless microphone. (B) The webinar had over three hundred viewers. (C) From two o’clock until three-thirty.

Why don’t we review the customer survey results before drafting next month’s campaign? (A) That’s a sensible idea—let’s meet after lunch. (B) Because the survey had ten questions. (C) At the marketing agency on Le Loi Street.

How many applicants were shortlisted for the senior analyst role? (A) Five candidates will be interviewed this week. (B) At least three years of financial experience. (C) In the human resources department.
How long will the server migration take tonight? (A) Roughly two hours, starting at midnight. (B) Since last October. (C) To improve database security.
Whose notebook was left on the conference table after the briefing? (A) I think it belongs to Minh from product design. (B) To take notes during the lecture. (C) Yes, the briefing went smoothly.
What time does the shuttle bus leave for the industrial park? (A) Every half hour starting at seven-fifteen. (B) Right outside the north gate. (C) It carries twenty-four passengers.
How much did the courier charge for same-day delivery? (A) Ninety thousand dong, including insurance. (B) By five o’clock this evening. (C) The package weighed three kilograms.

Do you know whether the training materials have been uploaded to the class portal? (A) The instructor posted all the slides this morning. (B) Yes, the train arrives at track two. (C) For the intermediate business English course.
Can you tell me where the visitor parking passes are kept? (A) The security guard at Desk A issues them. (B) Parking is free for two hours. (C) Because the underground lot is full.
May I borrow your laser pointer for my afternoon workshop? (A) Of course, just return it before five o’clock. (B) The workshop covers project management. (C) Point four on the agenda.

What did you think of the keynote speaker’s talk on sustainable packaging? (A) Her case studies on recyclable materials were very practical. (B) She spoke for forty minutes. (C) In the grand ballroom.
Has the facilities team announced when the elevator repair will be finished? (A) Service should resume by noon tomorrow. (B) Please use the stairs on the east side. (C) To replace a worn cable.
We are running low on A4 paper in the copy room. (A) I’ll bring two reams from the supply closet right away. (B) The copier was serviced last week. (C) Thirty pages per document.

Woman: Hi Daniel, I just checked the registration table for tomorrow’s Career Open House, and we only have forty printed name badges left.
Man: Really? Over ninety visitors registered online this week. Did the print shop deliver the second box?
Woman: Not yet. I called them ten minutes ago, and the courier is stuck in traffic near the bridge.
Man: In that case, let’s print temporary badges on the office laser printer for the first morning group so check-in isn’t delayed.

Man: Linh, have the regional sales reps tested the new mobile invoicing app yet?
Woman: Most of them have. They really like how fast it generates PDF receipts, but several reps in Da Nang reported that offline mode doesn’t sync automatically when Wi-Fi returns.
Man: That’s an important catch before next Monday’s company-wide rollout. Can your engineering team push a hotfix by Thursday?
Woman: Yes, we already identified the background timer bug and will release version 1.2 tomorrow afternoon.

Woman: Mr. Tran, our architectural firm finished the floor plan for your clinic’s second-floor expansion.
Man: Thank you, Mai. Let’s see—there are four consultation rooms here, but the waiting lounge looks smaller than we discussed.
Woman: We widened the hallway to meet the new municipal fire code. However, if we relocate the storage cabinets to the basement, we can add twelve square meters back to the lounge.
Man: That sounds much better. Please revise the drawing and send the cost estimate to my email.

Man: Excuse me, I bought this ergonomic office chair from your store on Saturday, but one of the armrest bolts is missing from the hardware kit.
Woman: I’m sorry about that, sir. Do you have your order receipt with you?
Man: Yes, here it is on my phone. Model Aero-Pro in charcoal gray.
Woman: Thank you. We have spare hardware packets behind the service counter, so I can hand you a complete bolt set right now, and I’ll also issue a ten-percent voucher for your next purchase.

Woman: Have you looked at the enrollment numbers for the Business Writing course starting next week?
Man: Yes, twenty-eight employees signed up, which exceeds our twenty-person classroom cap.
Woman: Should we open a second section on Thursday evenings?
Man: Instructor Clara is available on Thursday evenings, and Room 304 is free then. I’ll email the last eight registrants to offer them the Thursday slot.

Man: Ms. Le, our ceramic tableware shipment for the Kyoto hotel client is packed and ready at the port warehouse.
Woman: Great news. Is it still scheduled to sail on the Friday cargo vessel?
Man: Actually, customs clearance finished a day early, so the freight forwarder offered to load our containers onto Wednesday’s vessel at no extra cost.
Woman: Let’s accept that offer. Arriving two days early will give the hotel’s kitchen staff plenty of time to unpack before their grand opening.

Woman: Marcus, our company podcast episodes on personal finance have been downloaded over fifty thousand times this quarter.
Man: That’s double our initial target! Listeners especially liked the episode on budgeting for first-time homebuyers.
Woman: Since engagement is so strong, I’d like to invite a guest real-estate economist for a live question-and-answer episode next month.
Man: Good thinking. I know Dr. Minh Ngo at the Economics Institute—I can reach out to him today.

Man: Hello, this is Kenji Sato from Sato Biotech. We booked the Lotus Ballroom at your hotel for our annual symposium on November fifteenth.
Woman: Yes, Mr. Sato, I have your reservation right here for one hundred twenty guests.
Man: Two of our overseas panelists will now join remotely from Singapore, so we’ll need dual projection screens and a dedicated high-speed ethernet line.
Woman: Our audiovisual package includes dual screens, and I’ll ask our network technician to set up the wired connection in the ballroom.

Woman: We finished interviewing the final three candidates for the Quality Assurance Lead position this morning.
Man: Both Ms. Dao and Mr. Kiet had impressive automation portfolios. Who stood out to the panel?
Woman: Ms. Dao has five years of experience leading medical-device testing, which aligns directly with our new hospital software contract.
Man: I agree. Let’s prepare an offer letter for Ms. Dao before the end of the day so we can onboard her by the first of the month.

Man: Lan, the afternoon batch of aluminum water bottles just came off Coating Line B, and I noticed a slight color variation on the navy-blue lids.
Woman: Let me take a look. You’re right—the curing oven temperature drifted five degrees below specification.
Man: Should we halt Line B while we recalibrate the thermostat?
Woman: Yes, pause the conveyor for twenty minutes and set aside the last fifty units for secondary inspection.

Woman: Good morning, I’m calling from Greenleaf Publishing. Author Elena Rostova’s book-signing tour stops in your city on December fourth, and we’re looking for a venue.
Man: Our central bookstore café hosts author talks every month. How many attendees do you expect?
Woman: Around sixty readers. We also need a small table near the entrance for selling signed copies.
Man: Our mezzanine lounge seats seventy comfortably, and there’s a display counter right by the stairs. Let me send you our event booking agreement.

Man: Hi Thu, I submitted my travel expense report for the Hanoi trade fair last Tuesday, but the reimbursement hasn’t appeared in my bank account yet.
Woman: Let me pull up your file, David. Ah, the hotel receipt is attached, but the boarding passes for your return flight are missing.
Man: Oh, I accidentally uploaded the itinerary confirmation instead of the actual boarding passes.
Woman: If you upload the boarding pass PDF before noon today, I can include your claim in this Friday’s payroll transfer.

Woman: Kiet, the client for the Eco-Transit campaign asked us to update the poster headline and confirm the printing schedule.
Man: Which print package are they using for the subway stations?
Woman: They chose the weather-resistant vinyl format—Format B2 on the production sheet—because half the displays are on outdoor platforms.
Man: Got it. Format B2 takes forty-eight hours to laminate, so I’ll send the final artwork to the press by five o’clock today.

Hello Ms. Vu, this is Minh Phan calling from Lotus Banquet Services. I’m reviewing the refreshment order for your law firm’s seminar on Friday morning. Your online form lists forty boxed lunches, but only fifteen coffee carafes—which usually serves aboutone hundredfifty people, far more than forty. I suspect you meant to order five carafes instead of fifteen. Please call me back before four o’clock today so we can adjust your invoice before our kitchen orders the fresh pastries.

Attention passengers booked on Pacific Skyways Flight 418 to Busan. Due to a late-arriving aircraft from Taipei, departure has been pushed back by thirty-five minutes to six-twenty P.M. Also, please note that boarding has moved from Gate 14A to Gate 19B in the East Concourse. Complimentary bottled water and light snacks are available at the Gate 19B counter upon presentation of your boarding pass. Thank you for your patience.

Welcome to the Maritime Heritage Museum. My name is Ha, and I’ll be guiding your ninety-minute tour this morning. We’ll start here in the Shipbuilding Hall, where you can see a full-scale wooden trading vessel from the eighteenth century. Photography without flash is welcome in all galleries except the Ancient Maps Room on the upper deck, where light levels are strictly controlled. At eleven-thirty, we’ll conclude at the harbor terrace for a demonstration of traditional rope-making.

Before we wrap up our weekly editorial meeting, I want to congratulate everyone on the launch of our new Learning Hub portal. Traffic rose by forty percent in the first week. However, our reader support team noticed that many learners are searching for downloadable grammar checklists. Starting next month, each long-form article must include a one-page summary PDF. I’ve placed a standardized InDesign template in the shared editorial drive so your layout work stays consistent.

You’re listening to Metro Morning on 98.5 FM. If you’re commuting into the financial district today, please allow extra time. Water-main repairs have closed two eastbound lanes on Nguyen Hue Boulevard between Canal Street and Park Avenue until four P.M. City Transit has added extra express buses along the riverside highway, and commuters using the Metro Line 1 train will find normal five-minute frequency all morning. Stay tuned for our business market update after the break.

Thank you for visiting the SunWave booth at the Clean Energy Expo. What I’m holding is our new FoldLite solar charger, designed for field engineers and outdoor researchers. Unlike rigid solar panels, the FoldLite rolls up like a newspaper and weighs under four hundred grams. Even on overcast days, its high-efficiency silicon cells can charge a standard tablet to eighty percent in ninety minutes. Stop by our counter to scan the QR code for a fifteen-percent trade-show discount.

Good afternoon, everyone. This is a quick announcement from the Information Security desk. Tonight between ten P.M. and midnight, we will upgrade our virtual private network certificates. If you are working remotely this evening, please save all open documents on the shared cloud drive before nine-forty-five P.M. Tomorrow morning, when you sign in to your work laptop, a pop-up window will prompt you to enter your six-digit authenticator code once to activate the new certificate.

Welcome to Vertex Precision Electronics. Before we enter the clean-room assembly floor, please put on the antistatic smock, hairnet, and shoe covers provided in the locker area. Mobile phones and metal jewelry must remain locked in your visitor cabinet because electrostatic discharge can damage sensitive circuit boards. Throughout our walk, please stay within the yellow floor lines and hold any questions until we reach the observation lounge at the end of Corridor C.

Hello, Mr. Ngo, this is Sofia from Horizon Wellness Club. Thank you for signing up for our annual gold membership! Your member keycard is ready for pickup at our front desk any day between six A.M. and ten P.M. Remember that your membership includes two complimentary posture and fitness assessments with a certified trainer. Since evening appointments fill up two weeks in advance, I recommend booking your first session through the Horizon mobile app as soon as you activate your account.

Good evening, colleagues. It is my privilege to present this year’s Innovation Excellence Award to Dr. Bich Pham, head of our Sustainable Materials Lab. Over the past eighteen months, Dr. Pham and her six-person team developed a plant-based coating that replaces single-use plastic lining in takeaway beverage cups. Thanks to their breakthrough, three national café chains have already signed supply agreements with our company. Next month, Dr. Pham will travel to Geneva to represent us at the Global Packaging Forum.
